llm.summary: The skill's high-level claims (WhatsApp/Telegram ingestion, automatic privacy redaction) are not fully backed by the provided files — redaction logic and message-integration are promised but not implemented, and there are undeclared environment/network assumptions that may lead to data leakage if used as-is.

dimensions.detail: The skill advertises WhatsApp/Telegram → Obsidian ingestion, automatic privacy redaction, and local Ollama-based semantic search. However, there is no code that connects to WhatsApp/Telegram or performs message ingestion; provided scripts handle file sync and semantic search only. The privacy-redaction guarantee is described in prompts/docs but no implementation for detecting & replacing secrets is present in the scripts. This gap between claimed capability and actual code is a material incoherence.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions and prompts require reading/writing Obsidian files, performing Git pushes, and calling Ollama. The search engine and sync scripts do those file/network operations. Prompts assert mandatory redaction before pushing, but none of the shipped scripts perform content scanning/redaction — so the instructions rely on an enforcement mechanism that isn't present. The skill also references config edits (_meta.json) and local paths; these affect user files and require care.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec (instruction-only) — lower install risk. But the package includes executable scripts and a Python search utility that will be run on the user's host. Because there's no installer, files are intended to be run/linked by the user; that reduces supply-chain risk but means user will run code locally (audit recommended).
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Registry metadata declared no required env vars, but search_engine.py reads OLLAMA_BASE_URL and OLLAMA_MODEL from environment (defaults provided). The default OLLAMA_BASE_URL points to a LAN IP (http://192.168.3.120:11434), which is an odd hardcoded default and could indicate the developer's private test host. Git push requires credentials (ssh keys or git auth) though these are not mentioned explicitly. The prompts describe token detection patterns (ghp_, sk-, etc.) but there is no code implementing that detection — the skill asks for sensitive access (file read/write, exec) without demonstrable proportional safeguards.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Skill is not always:true and doesn't claim persistent elevated platform privileges. It requests exec/file read/write permissions in metadata, which are consistent with the declared functionality (reading Obsidian, running git). Autonomous invocation is allowed by default (platform behavior) but does not combine with other flagged privileges to produce a higher immediate risk vector.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
Key things to know before installing:

- Implementation gap: The README and prompts promise WhatsApp/Telegram ingestion and automatic privacy redaction, but no message-bridge code or redaction routines are present in the shipped scripts. Do not assume your secrets will be removed — the push scripts do not redact content.

- Verify and change defaults: search_engine.py defaults OLLAMA_BASE_URL to http://192.168.3.120:11434 (a private IP). Update OLLAMA_BASE_URL to your Ollama instance (e.g., http://localhost:11434) and verify the endpoint before use.

- Inspect and test: Manually review and test the code in a safe environment with non-sensitive sample notes. Confirm where and how redaction would run, or add an explicit content-sanitization step before enabling git sync.

- Git pushes and credentials: The push/sync scripts run git push and will transmit whatever is in your Obsidian vault to the configured remote. Ensure the remote is a private repo you control, and disable automatic pushes until you confirm redaction works. Use a throwaway repository when testing.

- Missing ingestion: If you expect WhatsApp/Telegram automatic ingestion, ask the author for the bridge/ingestion code (or implement your own). Without it, the skill only provides local file search and git sync utilities plus policy prompts.

- Minimal exposure: Run the skill in an isolated account/container or with a limited Obsidian folder to reduce blast radius. Do not point it at vaults that contain keys or sensitive material until you have verified redaction.

If you want, I can list exactly where to modify files (change OLLAMA_BASE_URL, add a redaction scan before git commit, or add a safe test procedure) or draft a simple redaction wrapper to run prior to push.
